Thanks, Vanessa and Lena. I reviewed the Starlance redlines this morning. High-level notes attached — I've converted the most material asks into three response options to keep negotiations flexible:

Option A (minimal change): Accept current DPA language, provide a brief addendum clarifying that Redwood will act as processor and that cross-border transfers use SCCs plus documented safeguards.

Option B (commercial middle ground): Add a short clause in the Order Form specifying the export-control responsibilities matrix (who handles export licenses, who notifies customers) and a 30-day SLA for sub-processor disclosure.

Option C (customer-favorable): Agree to an explicit role allocation in the DPA identifying Redwood as 'data processor' for processing activities and include a bespoke TIA addendum guaranteeing additional controls for transfers to US-hosted components.

I've attached a redline of the Order Form that introduces a responsibility matrix (spreadsheet reference) and a suggested paragraph for the DPA preamble to make roles explicit. From a risk perspective, Option B balances customer needs and our policy.

Attachments: suggested_orderform_redline.pdf

Action: Rishi — can you confirm whether Option B leaves any residual export-control obligations that we should escalate to Security?

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Counsel, Contracts

Agree with Karthik that Option B is the pragmatic path. Quick technical notes from a TIA/export-controls angle:

- Export controls: Our standard operating model does not require Redwood to take on export-license obligations for customer data — customers remain responsible for classifying data and requesting any export licensing. We can accept a notification and cooperation clause but should avoid hard license obligations.
- TIA: We can provide a CSV of non-EU sub-processors and a summary TIA (high-level controls) within 7 business days once procurement confirms scope. Drafting note: include "cooperation and assistance" language rather than "assume responsibility" phrasing.
- Evidence: David — can you confirm the ETA for the sub-processor CSV and whether we can include redacted site locations (yes/no)?

If Starlance needs a stronger contractual promise, we should confirm whether that is a deal point large enough to require a Commercial concession (discount/commitment). Vanessa — we should flag that for Sales.

Rishi

Redwood Inference
